discovery: The optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms enabling optical frequency measurement at the 10^-18 level

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock (2001-2005): trapping thousands of neutral atoms in an optical lattice at a 'magic' wavelength where the light shift of the clock transition cancels. This overturned the belief that confining atoms with light must perturb their frequency, combining the Lamb-Dicke regime of trapped ions with the signal-to-noise of large ensembles. Ye turned the concept into the world's most precise and stable clocks, using frequency combs, ultrastable lasers and quantum many-body control to reach 10^-18 and below, and to resolve the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample. Lattice clocks now drive the redefinition of the SI second, relativistic geodesy, and searches for dark matter and variation of fundamental constants. Building on the frequency-comb revolution recognised in 2005, this is the decisive step in precision measurement of our time.
